title: Cardiovascular effects of beta-agonists in patients with asthma and COPD: a meta-analysis
authors: Salpeter SR, Ormiston TM, Salpeter EE
population: 13 single-dose and 20 longer randomised placebo-controlled trials (3 days to 1 year) of beta2-agonists in asthma or COPD
funder: not read: the full text requires a subscription; the archived journal page shows the abstract and affiliations (Santa Clara Valley Medical Center; Cornell University) without a funding statement.
result: A single dose of beta2-agonist raised heart rate by 9.12 beats/min (95% CI 5.32 to 12.92) and lowered potassium by 0.36 mmol/l (0.18 to 0.54) against placebo. In trials of 3 days to 1 year, beta2-agonists increased the risk of a cardiovascular event (sinus or ventricular tachycardia, syncope, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, myocardial infarction, cardiac arrest or sudden death): RR 2.54 (1.59 to 4.05); sinus tachycardia alone RR 3.06 (1.70 to 5.50), all other events RR 1.66 (0.76 to 3.6). Longer trials were included only if they reported at least one adverse event.
